subject: Re: Oakridge - Data obliteration proof & residency mapping for SOC2 audit
messages:
From: Rachel Morris <rachel.morris@oakridgebank.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: ThirdParty Audit <audit@thirdpartyaudit.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data deletion proof request for SOC2 - Oakridge tenant

Hi Sean,

We're preparing for a SOC 2 readiness review next week and our external auditor (CC'd) has asked Redwood to provide evidence showing end-to-end deletion for our tenant (tenant id: OR-2034). Specifically they need:

- A manifest of deletion runs that touched OR-2034 between 2026-10-01 and 2026-11-25, including timestamps and operator/service that initiated the run.
- Proof that backups/snapshots containing tenant data were identified and purged (or retained under documented policy) — include snapshot manifests and whether snapshots were copied to cold storage or other regions.
- S3/object storage lifecycle policy and a sample object deletion record (with checksum/hash) and a list of object prefixes that map to OR-2034.
- Evidence for any cross-region replication copies and how those were removed.
- Records showing KMS keys used for encryption for the tenant, and whether key rotation or destruction impacted recoverability for deleted artifacts.
- Retention mapping that ties our contract TTLs to system enforcement points (where policy is enforced).
- A sample audit trail (log entries) that demonstrates a single tenant deletion workflow from the API request through to final erase, including cache invalidation and KV cache purge.

We need an initial artifact set by Nov 30 COB for the audit team. If there's anything that needs narrowing in scope (hosted vs. dedicated), flag it. The auditors may request hashes to verify integrity of the exported manifests.

Thanks — appreciate a quick confirmation of receipt and ETA.

Best,
Rachel Morris
Head of Compliance, Oakridge Bank
rachel.morris@oakridgebank.com
(415) 555-0192
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Morris <rachel.morris@oakridgebank.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, ThirdParty Audit <audit@thirdpartyaudit.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:05:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Data deletion proof request for SOC2 - Oakridge tenant

Hi Rachel — thanks for the detailed list and for looping in the auditors. Confirmed receipt.

Quick clarifying questions so we scope the artifacts correctly:
- Is the scope only for Redwood Hosted (our multi-tenant hosted offering) or do you also want artifacts for any Dedicated pools or on-prem instances tied to OR-2034?
- For time range: you listed 2026-10-01 to 2026-11-25. Do you want a broader window (e.g., 6 months) or exactly that window?

Planned deliverables (we'll produce these unless you ask us to narrow):
1) Deletion run manifest (CSV) with run_id, initiated_by, start_ts, end_ts, items_targeted (object prefixes & DB shard ids).
2) Snapshot manifest + snapshot deletion confirmations (manifest with snapshot ids + deletion timestamp + storage location).
3) Object-level deletion exports (sample of deleted keys with CRC32/SHA256 hashes, size, timestamp).
4) Cross-region replication purge notes (where applicable) and the replication config snapshot.
5) KMS usage summary for keys tied to OR-2034 and whether keys were rotated or scheduled; note: we do not destroy customer-managed KMS keys unless instructed.
6) Residency & retention mapping PDF that ties contractual TTLs to enforcement points (API, lifecycle policies, backup jobs).
7) Audit trail snippet showing the API request, internal job kickoff (worker_id), database erase marker, cache eviction event, and final confirmation.

Target timeline:
- Clarify scope today (we can accommodate Hosted-only with faster turnaround).
- Provide initial package (manifests + mapping PDF + sample logs) by Nov 29 EOD.
- Final package (hashes + full CSV export) by Nov 30 COB.

Lauren and Neha from Legal & Security are on the CC for any redlines on what we can share. Neha — can your team check whether we need to pseudonymize any object keys or mask account IDs before sending to the auditor?

Rachel, is delivery via secure upload to your shared S3 / the DocuSign-style link acceptable? We will also provide hash sums for tamper-evidence.

Thanks,

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 646 555 0118
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: ThirdParty Audit <audit@thirdpartyaudit.com>, Rachel Morris <rachel.morris@oakridgebank.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:23:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Data deletion proof request for SOC2 - Oakridge tenant

Hi Rachel / Audit team —

Technical clarifications from Security so the evidence set is usable for your controls testing:
- We will provide a deletion_export CSV (sample and full) that includes a canonical mapping from object prefixes to tenant logical IDs. If you need tenant IDs redacted, tell us which fields to mask.
- For snapshots: our manifest will include snapshot_id, creation_ts, stored_region, and deletion_ts. Note that snapshot retention for long-term cold archives may be governed by a separate archival SLA; if OR-2034 used any archival overrides, we will flag them.
- Backups: nightly backups that contain tenant data are retained for N days per contract; we will include backup job ids and retention windows. For any backup that was destroyed as part of the deletion we will provide an erase marker and the worker job log.
- Replication: where cross-region replication exists, we will include the replication policy + confirmation of purge. For replicated DB shards we will include the shard decommission log entries.
- For KMS: we'll provide an audit of API calls to the KMS for keys associated with the tenant. Note: we cannot provide raw KMS private material.

Attachments we'll upload in the next update: deletion_export_2026-11-25.csv (full run manifest), snapshot_manifest_2026-11-01.txt (snapshots referenced), and a short audit_hashes_20261129.txt with SHA256 sums. Also attaching a residency_retention_mapping_v3.pdf mapping contract TTLs to enforcement points.

We will stage the artifacts to a secure bucket and provide pre-signed links to the auditors and to Oakridge. If any artifacts need additional redaction, call them out and we'll produce a masked sample quickly.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0147
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Morris <rachel.morris@oakridgebank.com>, ThirdParty Audit <audit@thirdpartyaudit.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 15:46:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Data deletion proof request for SOC2 - Oakridge tenant

Rachel / Audit team —

Attached is the package we discussed. Summary of contents below and where each artifact maps to your original asks: 

Attachments (uploaded to secure bucket; local copies attached here):
- deletion_export_2026-11-25.csv — full manifest for OR-2034 deletion jobs run on 2026-11-25 (columns: run_id, tenant_id, object_prefix, object_key, size_bytes, sha256, start_ts, end_ts, worker_id).
- snapshot_manifest_2026-11-01.txt — snapshot ids that previously contained tenant data and their deletion confirmations (includes storage region column).
- audit_hashes_20261129.txt — SHA256 hashes for the CSV and manifest files (signed by our internal artifact signing key).
- residency_retention_mapping_v3.pdf — mapping of contractual TTLs to enforcement points (API enforcement, S3 lifecycle, backup retention).

Key notes / limitations:
- Hosted vs Dedicated: package covers our Hosted environment only. If you need Dedicated/on-prem evidence, please confirm the dedicated pool ids and we will scope those artifacts separately.
- Cold archives: one snapshot (snap-202605) was migrated to a cold archive in a partner vault under an archival SLA; we flagged that snapshot in the manifest. We have a documented process for requesting archival purge from the partner and will share the request ticket on receipt of your confirmation.
- KMS: We included an extract of KMS API calls tied to tenant key usage; we cannot provide private key material.

For traceability we also included line-level worker logs for the relevant deletion jobs (in the secure bucket). If the auditor wants, we can provide a small, redacted sample showing the full end-to-end workflow (API request -> job queue -> worker -> DB marker -> cache eviction -> job confirmation) and the exact log line timestamps.

Please confirm receipt and whether the artifacts satisfy the auditor's test cases; happy to jump on a short call if you want to walk through any of the files.

Thanks,
Sean

Attachments: deletion_export_2026-11-25.csv (attachment), snapshot_manifest_2026-11-01.txt (attachment), audit_hashes_20261129.txt (attachment), residency_retention_mapping_v3.pdf (attachment)
